summary: Learn spatial finance, satellite screening, and ESG portfolio monitoring. Build practical risk outputs for credit, investment, and reporting decisions.
lede: Spatial finance connects geospatial evidence with financial decisions, helping teams identify how land use, deforestation, water stress, and infrastructure encroachment may affect asset value, repayment capacity, and investor confidence. This course provides a structured workflow for geocoding assets, joining location data to loans or investments, screening exposure, assessing materiality, and documenting escalation decisions. You will work with Google Earth Engine concepts, QGIS workflows, satellite imagery, and supplied datasets to develop indicators, portfolio heatmaps, risk registers, monitoring thresholds, and evidence packs. The course also explores how the Equator Principles, IFC Performance Standards, and TNFD can support analysis and reporting for agriculture, mining, infrastructure, and other land-intensive activities.
audienceIntro: Spatial finance training suits professionals who connect environmental and social evidence with lending, investment, supervision, or portfolio reporting decisions. You can apply the methods with operational GIS or financial risk experience, while the course also provides structured foundations for professionals moving into location-based risk analysis.
modules: Spatial Finance Foundations and Portfolio Exposure
Geocoding, Data Quality, and Spatial Joins
Geospatial Integration with Credit and ESG Models
prerequisites: You should have working exposure to ESG risk, credit analysis, investment portfolio review, sustainability reporting, GIS, or environmental and social due diligence. No programming experience is required, and you do not need to build production remote-sensing models. Familiarity with spreadsheets and basic map interpretation will help you complete the exercises efficiently. Advanced satellite analytics and AI-assisted change detection receive conceptual or operational coverage rather than technical engineering instruction.
